title: ASPIRe: the SFC's virtual-asset roadmap
md:
The Securities and Futures Commission's (SFC's) February 2025 roadmap of five pillars and 12 initiatives for Hong Kong's virtual-asset (VA) market. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | SFC [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (roadmap); several initiatives since delivered through SFC circulars and guidance [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]; [S:f09e57feb89b, paras 2, 4]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2] |
| Started | 19 Feb 2025 [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| Next official date | H2 2026: SFC digital-asset custody surveillance system to begin operating (stated target in the Policy Address) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| Covered in | [A3](#m-A3), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [C6](#m-C6), [C7](#m-C7), [E1](#m-E1) |
## What it is

ASPIRe stands for five pillars: Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure and Relationships. Together they hold 12 initiatives. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] Access covers new licensing regimes for VA over-the-counter (OTC) dealing and custody; legislative preparation for custodians was aimed for completion by end-2025. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1] Safeguards includes exploring technology-neutral, outcome-based custody standards and a more flexible approach to cold-storage ratios. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] Products looks at new token listings and derivatives for professional investors, margin financing, staking, and borrowing and lending. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar P, Initiatives 6-8] Infrastructure covers regulatory reporting and surveillance tools such as wallet tracing. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar I, Initiative 9] Many initiatives are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19 Feb 2025 | ASPIRe roadmap published | Exploratory | [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 1] |
| 7 Apr 2025 | Staking guidance for VA trading platforms (VATPs) and VA funds, framed under Pillar P | In force | [S:36753b22e10a, para 2, Note 2] |
| 27 Jun 2025 | VA dealing and custodian consultations (Pillar A); conclusions published 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1]; [S:6186c01c6649, Introduction, p.3 and fn 2] |
| 15 Aug 2025 | SFC custody circular to VATPs cites Pillar S, Initiative 3 | In force | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Importance of resilient custody controls and expected standards' section, p.1] |
| 3 Nov 2025 | Shared order book and product-expansion circulars (Pillars A and P) | In force | [S:f09e57feb89b, paras 2, 4] |
| 11 Feb 2026 | VA financing, perpetual contracts framework and affiliated market makers | Issued | [S:089ec86e2407, paras 1-4] |
| H2 2026 | SFC digital-asset custody surveillance system to begin operating | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |
| 2027 | CrypTech components for market and anti-money laundering (AML) surveillance, using big data | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- The SFC describes the roadmap as an evolving plan, not a final destination. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 5] Its initiatives take effect through separate circulars and guidance, such as those on staking and VA financing. [S:36753b22e10a, paras 2-3]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2]
- VA financing now reaches banks too. Registered institutions (RIs) providing VA dealing services may offer financing for VA dealing to their securities margin clients, following standards similar to the SFC's. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', items (1)-(2)]
- Intermediaries, including RIs, may offer staking to clients they deal in VAs for, but should use only segregated accounts held at an SFC-licensed platform or at an authorized financial institution. [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4-5]
- Under the SFC's framework, VATP perpetual contracts should be offered only to professional investors. Margin collateral should be fiat money, or Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)-regulated stablecoins or tokenised deposits. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']
- Pillar A's OTC and custody plans became proposed VA dealing and custodian regimes. Banks would register rather than be licensed, with the HKMA as frontline regulator. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]; [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4] Two further proposed regimes, for VA advisory and VA management, would also let only banks register. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 52, 58 and fns 9-10]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** ASPIRe is a roadmap; its initiatives take effect through separate SFC circulars and guidance, so track those. [S:cfe8a53186c3, para 5]; [S:089ec86e2407, para 2]
- **To business heads:** Delivered items so far include staking, shared order books, VA financing and professional-investor perpetuals. [S:36753b22e10a, para 2]; [S:f09e57feb89b, para 2]; [S:089ec86e2407, paras 2-3]
- **To the CEO:** The SFC's Executive Director of Intermediaries called the roadmap-based approach essential to scaling Hong Kong's digital asset market. [S:089ec86e2407, para 5]
- **To Risk:** Outcome-based custody standards are still framed as something to explore; the SFC's August 2025 VATP custody circular took immediate effect. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]; [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7]

2. SFC sets out new roadmap to develop Hong Kong as a global virtual asset hub — SFC — 19 Feb 2025 — read paras 1-3 — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/news-and-announcements/news/doc?refNo=25PR20
3. SFC launches trading initiatives to boost digital asset market vibrancy in Hong Kong — SFC — 11 Feb 2026 — read paras 2-4 — https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/news-and-announcements/news/doc?refNo=26PR24
4. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — HKSAR Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read paras 49 and 51(iii) — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

title: Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) and amended CRS
md:
Hong Kong's bill to bring in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) yearly crypto-asset tax reporting standard and to update the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) that Hong Kong has applied since 2018. [S:252a7f86684e, paras 2-4]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and Inland Revenue Department (IRD) [S:275d5cc93a88, Foreword, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Bill before LegCo (gazetted 22 May 2026; First Reading 3 Jun 2026) [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Started | Commitment to the OECD Global Forum, 13 Dec 2024 [S:ea81f92ea327, para 1] |
| Next official date | 1 Jan 2027: CARF duties start, if the bill passes [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] |
| Covered in | [D5](#m-D5), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

CARF is an OECD standard for yearly automatic exchange of crypto-asset tax information between jurisdictions. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 2] Hong Kong aimed to have its law in place by 2026 and to start exchanges from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] The bill defines a reporting crypto-asset service provider (RCASP) as a person that, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers. That includes acting as counterparty or intermediary, or offering a trading platform. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"] An RCASP with a Hong Kong nexus would have to register, carry out due diligence, file returns and keep records. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50O-50Q, 50S] Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and specified e-money products are outside CARF but are brought into the amended CRS. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3] If passed, CARF starts on 1 January 2027 and amended CRS on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13 Dec 2024 | Hong Kong commits to CARF; first exchanges from 2028 | Stated target | [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4] |
| 9 Dec 2025 | FSTB–IRD consultation (to 6 Feb 2026) | Superseded | [S:252a7f86684e, paras 1, 7]; [S:275d5cc93a88, Foreword, para 1] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget: amendment bill in the first half of 2026 | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108] |
| 22 May 2026 | Bill gazetted | Bill before LegCo | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| 3 Jun 2026 | First Reading; Second Reading debate adjourned | Bill before LegCo | [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| 1 Jan 2027 | Part 2 (CARF) commences, if passed | Bill before LegCo | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] |
| 1 Jan 2028 | Part 3 (amended CRS) commences, if passed | Bill before LegCo | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Under the bill, any group entity that, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers, including as an intermediary, would be an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- The Hong Kong nexus tests cover tax residence, incorporation, management, a regular place of business, and Hong Kong branches. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- A Hong Kong RCASP would have to register by 31 January of the year after it first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)]
- RCASPs would need tax-residence self-certifications from new customers, and from existing users within 12 months of the rules taking effect. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- Under the amended CRS, crypto-linked derivatives count as financial assets, and CBDCs and specified e-money products are added to the depository-account definition. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.4]
- Registration and returns would go to the IRD through its planned CARF Portal. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']
- Engaging a service provider would not, on its own, be a reasonable excuse for failing to register, do due diligence or file returns. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The bill is not yet law. If passed, CARF duties start 1 January 2027 and amended CRS 1 January 2028. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]
- **To business heads:** A customer crypto exchange service run as a business, even as intermediary, can make the entity an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- **To the CEO:** Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024, with first data exchanges targeted from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
- **To Risk:** Proposed fines can scale: a further $500 a day for some continuing offences after conviction, and for due-diligence offences the higher of a level 3 fine or $1,000 per affected user or controlling person. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]

## Key documents

2. Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework page — IRD — undated — read the Overview, due diligence, registration and penalty sections — https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/dta_carf.htm
3. Implementation of CARF and Amendments in Relation to CRS (consultation paper) — FSTB and IRD — 9 Dec 2025 — read paras 4.3-4.18 and Chapter 6 — https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/government/publication/consultation/docs/2026/crypto-framework.pdf
4. Hong Kong commits to implementing Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework — FSTB — 13 Dec 2024 — read paras 1-4 — https://www.info.gov.hk/gia/general/202412/13/P2024121300491.htm

title: CBDC research and cross-border digital money pilots
md:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA's) research projects on central bank digital currency (CBDC) and tokenised money (Aurum, Sela, Genesis, Inthanon-LionRock), plus the cross-boundary e-CNY (digital renminbi) pilot and the 2026 Shanghai cooperation. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects' and 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' sections]; [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1]; [S:eb28508e5032, para 1]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA, with the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub (BISIH), other central banks and Mainland bodies [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1]; [S:eb28508e5032, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Research (Aurum, Sela, Genesis); Pilot (e-CNY); Exploratory (Shanghai memorandum of understanding, MoU) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)-(2)]; [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| Started | Q4 2019 (Inthanon-LionRock) [S:6b0fae230518, footnote 1] |
| Next official date | None stated; plans to upgrade e-CNY wallets and raise limits have no finalised timetable [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (2)] |
| Covered in | [E2](#m-E2), [C5](#m-C5), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

Project Aurum, with the BISIH and a local research institute, built a two-tier prototype. It paired a wholesale interbank system with retail e-wallets, and its report came out in October 2022. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] Project Sela, with the Bank of Israel, tested letting non-bank intermediaries, called Access Enablers, connect directly to a central bank's CBDC ledger. [S:8146b4a87d45, paras 2 and 5] Sela's report says it reflects no HKMA policy decision on a potential e-HKD. [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5] Project Genesis built prototype platforms for green bond tokenisation with the BISIH. [S:5a9cad53f2be, footnote 4] It concluded in 2021, and the Government's 2023 tokenised green bond built on it. [S:a0841967c871, quote from Eddie Yue] Inthanon-LionRock, with the Bank of Thailand, studied CBDC for cross-border payments and grew into mBridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and footnote 1] The cross-boundary e-CNY pilot lets Hong Kong residents set up personal e-CNY wallets with a Hong Kong mobile number and top them up through the Faster Payment System (FPS). [S:08caafe0cfe7, paras 1-2; Annex 1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2019 | Inthanon-LionRock begins with the Bank of Thailand | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, footnote 1] |
| 2021 | Project Genesis concluded | Research | [S:a0841967c871, quote from Eddie Yue] |
| Oct 2022 | Project Aurum report | Research | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] |
| 12 Sep 2023 | Project Sela report | Research | [S:8146b4a87d45, paras 1-2] |
| 20 Oct 2023 | HKMA sets up CBDC Expert Group with five local universities | Research | [S:28af6d5e86cb, para 1] |
| 17 May 2024 | Cross-boundary e-CNY pilot expanded | Pilot | [S:08caafe0cfe7, para 1] |
| 8 Oct 2025 | Government: e-CNY wallet upgrade still under discussion | Pilot | [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5)] |
| 2 Mar 2026 | MoU of the HKMA, Shanghai Data Bureau and a national blockchain centre on digitised cargo trade and finance | Exploratory | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| 25 Mar 2026 | Government reports about 80,000 e-CNY wallets and 18 top-up banks | Pilot | [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Sela's report says the project reflects no HKMA policy decision on a potential e-HKD. [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5]
- Pilot wallets are tier-4 personal wallets. Limits are RMB10,000 balance, RMB2,000 per transaction, RMB5,000 a day and RMB50,000 a year, with no person-to-person transfers. Operating institutions may set lower limits. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2, pp.1-2]
- In Hong Kong, 18 local banks support FPS top-ups. The PBoC (People's Bank of China) and the HKMA are exploring wallet upgrades to raise limits, but proposals and timing are not finalised. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)-(2)]
- Under the Shanghai MoU, cross-border financial cooperation and electronic bills of lading will be explored under Project Ensemble. Trade finance using cargo and trade data will be studied through linked data platforms. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
- The Government says stablecoins, CBDCs such as e-CNY, and tokenised deposits each have their own features and maturity. Market forces will largely decide their prospects. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (3)]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Sela and Aurum were research projects. Sela's report says it reflects no HKMA policy decision on an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects']; [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 1, footnote 5, p.5]
- **To business heads:** About 80,000 e-CNY wallets had been registered by end-January 2026, with 18 Hong Kong banks supporting FPS top-ups. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]
- **To the CEO:** Under the 2026 Shanghai MoU, electronic bills of lading will be explored under Project Ensemble. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]
- **To Risk:** Pilot e-CNY wallets do not allow person-to-person transfers and cap balances at RMB10,000. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2, pp.1-2]

title: CMU OmniClear digital asset platform and tokenised Exchange Fund Bills
md:
Plans for a digital asset platform run by the operator of the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), Hong Kong's central securities depository, and for HKMA tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | CMU OmniClear Limited, which operates the CMU on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA); HKMA for the Exchange Fund Bills tests [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-3]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Stated target [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| Started | CMU OmniClear set up 18 Oct 2024 [S:d43a14fd959f, para 1] |
| Next official date | Platform "this year" (2026); Exchange Fund Bills tests by year-end 2026 (both stated targets) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

CMU OmniClear was set up, wholly owned by the Exchange Fund, to run the CMU under a contract with the HKMA. [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-2] The HKMA stays the owner and system operator of the CMU, holds the legal relationships with CMU participants and makes CMU policy decisions. [S:d43a14fd959f, para 3]; [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 6] Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) is taking a 20% stake in the holding company, CMU OmniClear Holdings; the Exchange Fund keeps 80%. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] The 2026-27 Budget said CMU OmniClear would set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for digital bond issuance and settlement. It would later be extended to other digital assets and linked to other tokenisation platforms in the region. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] The 2026 Policy Address repeats the platform target. It also says the HKMA will test tokenising Exchange Fund Bills by year-end, so that banks can use the more than $1.3 trillion of these bills at any hour. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation's (HKMC's) June 2026 digital bonds were created on a CMU-operated distributed ledger technology (DLT) platform, with the CMU as clearing and settlement system. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 4]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Feb 2023 | First tokenised Government bond clears through the CMU with statutory finality | Issued | [S:a0841967c871, paras 1, 4] |
| 18 Oct 2024 | HKMA establishes CMU OmniClear Limited | In force | [S:d43a14fd959f, para 1] |
| 4 Mar 2025 | CMU OmniClear–HKEX memorandum of understanding (MoU) on post-trade infrastructure | Exploratory | [S:74db8f7570bd, paras 1-2] |
| 12 Nov 2025 | HKEX to take 20% of CMU OmniClear Holdings | Announced | [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget: digital asset platform to be set up in 2026 | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] |
| 10 Jun 2026 | HKMC digital bonds priced, created on a CMU-operated DLT platform | Issued | [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 4] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: platform this year; tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests by year-end | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Nothing binding yet. Both items are stated targets, and no platform rulebook or test design appears in the sources reviewed. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
- The Policy Address links the Exchange Fund Bills tests to banks' asset and liability management. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- Issuing on a CMU-operated DLT platform satisfies one of the two alternative Basic Requirements of the Digital Bond Grant Scheme; the HKMA decides case by case whether a platform counts. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2 and fn 6, p.3]
- The CMU is deemed a designated clearing and settlement system, so its settlements have statutory finality. Another DLT platform gets that only if the HKMA designates it; otherwise parties can agree finality by contract. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15]
- The HKMA's February 2024 tokenised-products circular does not cover products regulated under the Securities and Futures Ordinance; those follow the relevant Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and HKMA requirements. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** No rules have been published yet for the platform or the Exchange Fund Bills tests; both are stated targets. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)]
- **To business heads:** The platform is meant as a one-stop service for digital bond issuance and settlement. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA plans tests by end-2026 on tokenising Exchange Fund Bills, aimed at helping banks use more than $1.3 trillion of these bills round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- **To Risk:** A DLT platform has statutory finality only if the HKMA designates it; otherwise finality rests on contract. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 37-38, p.15]

## Key documents

1. The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address — HKSAR Government — 16 Sep 2026 — read para 35 (pp.22-23) — https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf
2. 2026-27 Budget — Financial Secretary — 25 Feb 2026 — read paras 112-114 — https://www.budget.gov.hk/2026/eng/pdf/e_budget_speech_2026-27.pdf
3. HKMA Establishes CMU OmniClear Limited — HKMA — 18 Oct 2024 — read paras 1-3 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/10/20241018-5/

title: Digital Bond Grant Scheme (DBGS)
md:
An HKMA subsidy that refunds part of the cost of issuing a digital bond in Hong Kong. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1; s.1, p.2]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (initial three-year period) [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| Started | Applications opened 28 Nov 2024; bonds issued on or after 16 Oct 2024 can apply [S:633ce27d4f9b, paras 1, 3]; [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 fn 1] |
| Next official date | End of the initial three years from 28 Nov 2024 (no renewal decision in the sources reviewed) [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 3] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The DBGS refunds half of eligible issuance costs for a digital bond. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] The cap is HK$1.25 million for a Half Grant, where only the Basic Requirements are met. It rises to HK$2.5 million for a Full Grant, where all Additional Requirements are also met. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] Each issuer, counted together with its associates, can receive grants for no more than two issues. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2] To qualify at all, half or more of the lead arrangers must be recognised arrangers. The bond also needs either a distributed ledger technology (DLT) team with substantial Hong Kong presence, or issuance on a DLT platform operated by the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU). [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3] The HKMA reserves the absolute right to decide whether requirements are met and how much to grant, and may adjust the scheme. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Oct 2024 | Scheme announced in the Policy Address; bonds issued from this date can apply | Announced | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1 fn 1] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | HKMA launches the DBGS and opens applications | In force | [S:633ce27d4f9b, paras 1, 3] |
| 28 Nov 2024 | Guideline on the DBGS issued | In force | [S:5a0563de8142, p.1] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget says the HKMA will use the DBGS to encourage more digital bond issues | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97] |
| 16 Jul 2026 | HKMA one-page scheme summary published | Reference | [S:2397140df663, p.1] |
| Nov 2027 | Initial three-year period ends (three years from 28 Nov 2024) | Stated period | [S:633ce27d4f9b, para 3] |

## What it means for your bank

- If the bank arranges bonds, arranger roles matter: half or more of the lead arrangers must be recognised arrangers for the issue to qualify. [S:5a0563de8142, s.2, p.3]
- The Full Grant needs a DLT platform provider outside the issuer's circle of associates. A bank issuing on its own group's platform would not meet that test. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4; s.1 fn 3, p.2]
- The Full Grant also needs at least HK$1 billion in size, five or more investors not associated with the issuer or platform provider, and a listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) or on a virtual asset trading platform that holds a Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licence. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]
- Fees paid to DLT platform providers or arrangers that are associates of the issuer are not eligible expenses, nor are costs covered by other grant schemes. [S:5a0563de8142, s.4 and fn 7, p.5]
- A green digital bond can claim general issuance costs under the DBGS or Track I of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, not both. [S:5a0563de8142, s.4, p.5]
- A formal application may be made within three months after issue. An optional pre-application consultation with the HKMA is available before or after issue. [S:5a0563de8142, s.5, p.6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The grant is a subsidy. The HKMA reserves the absolute right to decide eligibility and the amount. [S:5a0563de8142, p.1]
- **To business heads:** Clients can recover half of eligible expenses, up to HK$2.5 million per issue, for at most two issues per issuer and its associates. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1, p.2]
- **To the CEO:** The 2026-27 Budget says the HKMA will use the scheme to encourage more digital bond issues in Hong Kong. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97]
- **To Risk:** Using a DLT platform provided by an associate of the issuer rules out the Full Grant, leaving the Half Grant at most. [S:5a0563de8142, s.3, p.4]

## Key documents

1. Guideline on the Digital Bond Grant Scheme — HKMA — 28 Nov 2024 — read ss.1-5 on amounts, conditions, expenses and timing — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/bond-market-development/Guideline_on_the_Digital_Bond_Grant_Scheme.pdf
2. HKMA launches Digital Bond Grant Scheme — HKMA — 28 Nov 2024 — read paras 1-3 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2024/11/20241128-3/

title: Digital bonds: Genesis, Evergreen and the public-sector issues
md:
Hong Kong's run of bond tokenisation work, from the 2021 Project Genesis test to three Government green bond deals and the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation's (HKMC's) 2026 digital bond. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the HKSAR Government's representative for its bonds; HKMC for its own issue [S:a0841967c871, para 5]; [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Issued (latest issue dated 15 Jun 2026); the Policy Address says digital bond issuance will be regularised [S:6aa27ee8b400, Annex]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(i)] |
| Started | 2021 (Project Genesis proof of concept) [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7] |
| Next official date | No date given; the Budget says tokenised bonds will keep being issued on a regular basis [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 97] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [E2](#m-E2), [A3](#m-A3), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The HKMA began bond tokenisation in 2021 with a proof of concept run jointly with the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] Under Project Evergreen, the HKMA then helped the Government issue tokenised green bonds. [S:64cf94cf2036, para 2] The first, a HK$800 million bond in February 2023, was described as the first tokenised green bond issued by any government. [S:a0841967c871, para 1] It settled on a T+1 basis through the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), which carries statutory settlement finality. [S:a0841967c871, paras 3-4] The HKMA's August 2023 report found that no Hong Kong statute it reviewed prescribes the form debt securities must take at issuance. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 28, p.12] A multi-currency issue of about HK$6 billion followed in February 2024. [S:4290ec1111e3, para 1] In November 2025 a HK$10 billion issue became the first digital bond to offer settlement in tokenised central bank money (e-HKD and e-CNY). [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 1, 8] In June 2026 the HKMC priced about HK$12 billion of digital bonds, created on a CMU-operated distributed ledger technology (DLT) platform. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 1, 4]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | Project Genesis proof of concept with the BIS Innovation Hub | Research | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5]; [S:4290ec1111e3, para 7] |
| 31 Oct 2022 | Policy Statement names a tokenised green bond pilot | Historical | [S:f587b828e3fa, para 10(b)] |
| 16 Feb 2023 | HK$800m tokenised Government green bond settles | Issued | [S:a0841967c871, para 1; summary terms, 'Settlement'] |
| 24 Aug 2023 | HKMA report "Bond Tokenisation in Hong Kong" released | Research | [S:b7e1bb6b44ae, para 1] |
| 7 Feb 2024 | About HK$6bn multi-currency digital green bonds offered | Issued | [S:4290ec1111e3, para 1] |
| By 28 Nov 2024 | EvergreenHub knowledge repository launched | Launched | [S:64cf94cf2036, para 8] |
| 10 Nov 2025 | HK$10bn digital green bonds priced, with e-HKD/e-CNY settlement option | Issued | [S:ac6cd085a325, paras 2, 8] |
| 10 Jun 2026 | HKMC prices about HK$12bn digital bonds (issue date 15 Jun 2026) | Issued | [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1; Annex] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: digital bond issuance to be regularised | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(i)] |

## What it means for your bank

- In Evergreen, only custodians that were CMU participants and onboarded to the platform could open token accounts. Other investors held through those custodians, with their interests recorded in the custodians' own books. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 45, p.16]
- Where investors are onboarded to a platform, the report says the starting point is for the operator (and custodians, as appropriate) to run know-your-customer (KYC) checks and support anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) compliance. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 44, p.16]
- The CMU is deemed a designated clearing and settlement system, so its settlements have statutory finality. Another DLT platform gets that only if the HKMA designates it; otherwise parties can agree finality by contract. [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 36-38, pp.14-15]
- The report says the existing securities licensing and offering regimes under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO) also apply to issuing or distributing digital bonds. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11]
- The HKMA's February 2024 tokenised-products circular does not cover products regulated under the SFO; those follow the relevant SFC and HKMA requirements, such as the SFC's November 2023 tokenised securities circular. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage' and fn 2, p.1]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** The Evergreen report says existing SFO licensing and offering rules also apply to digital bonds. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 23, p.11]
- **To business heads:** Sixteen financial institutions arranged the HKMC deal. Investors could use existing CMU links to Euroclear and Clearstream, and settlement fell from T+5 to T+3. [S:6aa27ee8b400, paras 5, 8]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address says Hong Kong-issued digital bonds took nearly half the global market from 2025 to mid-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35]
- **To Risk:** The Evergreen report notes that DLT platform capabilities are largely untested in financial markets and suggests continuity plans, including for migrating to another platform. [S:a0b44be27c40, para 47, p.17]

## Key documents

1. Bond Tokenisation in Hong Kong (Project Evergreen report) — HKMA — 24 Aug 2023 — read paras 23-47 on law, custody and settlement — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2023/20230824e3a1.pdf
2. HKSAR Government's Third Digital Green Bonds Offering — HKMA — 11 Nov 2025 — read paras 1-10 and key features — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251111-6/
3. HKMC's HK$12 billion inaugural public digital bond issuance — HKMC (via HKMA) — 11 Jun 2026 — read paras 1-5 and the Annex — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/06/20260611-3/
4. EvergreenHub digital bond knowledge repository — HKMA — updated Jul 2026 — use as a reference index — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/key-functions/international-financial-centre/bond-market-development/digital-bond-knowledge-repository/

title: e-HKD (digital Hong Kong dollar)
md:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA's) long-running work on a possible Hong Kong central bank digital currency (CBDC), now focused on wholesale use by financial institutions. [S:d51dc8884c8a, opening paragraph]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Research (retail: groundwork done, no launch decision); wholesale use is the stated priority [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates'; 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] |
| Started | 2017 (Project LionRock) [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| Next official date | 2026: real-value e-HKD payments for after-hours derivatives trading with Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing (HKEX) (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |
| Covered in | [E2](#m-E2), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The HKMA began in 2017 with Project LionRock, a proof of concept on large-value payments and delivery-versus-payment settlement. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] It then consulted on a retail e-HKD through a 2021 technical paper and a 2022 policy paper. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'HKMA's Policy Stance on e-HKD used in retail applications'] The technical paper proposed a two-tier model in which commercial banks distribute e-HKD, and said it was not a blueprint. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4] In September 2022 the HKMA set out a three-rail approach. Its initial legal research suggested existing law may not give enough certainty to issue a digital form of legal tender. [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.10] Industry pilots ran in two phases, and the project was renamed e-HKD+ in September 2024 to cover tokenised deposits too. [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] In October 2025 the HKMA said the near-term priority lies beyond retail, in wholesale payments. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] It has not decided if, or when, it will introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | Project LionRock wholesale proof of concept | Research | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] |
| 4 Oct 2021 | Technical paper proposes two-tier design | Superseded | [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-5] |
| 27 Apr 2022 | Policy and design paper | Research | [S:3b42966a786e, Sections 1 and 7] |
| 20 Sep 2022 | Three-rail approach set | Research | [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.9] |
| 18 May 2023 | Phase 1 pilots start with 16 firms | Research | [S:933b9f10e3b2, para 1] |
| 30 Oct 2023 | Phase 1 report | Research | [S:9f8886b0fb21, Executive Summary, p.6] |
| 23 Sep 2024 | Phase 2 starts; project renamed e-HKD+ | Research | [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] |
| 28 Oct 2025 | Phase 2 report; wholesale uses prioritised | Research | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] |
| 11 Nov 2025 | Government digital green bonds offer an e-HKD settlement option | Issued | [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money' paragraph] |
| H1 2026 | Target to finish groundwork for possible retail use; the HKMA's CBDC page now says this work is completed | Research | [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 5]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates'] |
| 2026 | Real-value e-HKD payments for after-hours derivatives trading with HKEX | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 36(v)] |

## What it means for your bank

- The HKMA has made no policy decision on if, or when, an e-HKD would be introduced. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach'] The 2021 technical paper says its design is not a blueprint for e-HKD. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary point 4]
- The April 2022 paper said full anonymity is not a plausible option because of anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) requirements. It noted that tiered wallets are a common answer. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 1, p.4; Section 5.3, p.34]
- The same paper said that in a two-tier model, customer-facing institutions could be tasked with customer due diligence and record-keeping. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]
- Phase 2 found the public sees e-HKD and tokenised deposits in a similar light, because of high trust in banks. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 3]
- The HKMA says it will publish common token standards from the e-HKD Industry Forum. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 6]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** No decision exists to introduce an e-HKD. The 2022 paper saw distributing institutions as the ones that could handle customer due diligence. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']; [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]
- **To business heads:** The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale payments, supporting tokenisation and cross-border settlement. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- **To the CEO:** The Government's November 2025 digital green bonds were the first digital bond offering worldwide to use e-HKD and e-CNY (the Mainland's digital renminbi) in settlement. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money' paragraph]
- **To Risk:** In Phase 2, zero-knowledge proof privacy tools made transactions up to 320 times more expensive in gas fees (network transaction fees). [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', PDF p.34]

2. HKMA completes e-HKD Pilot Programme and outlines future direction of e-HKD — HKMA — 28 Oct 2025 — read paras 3-6 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/10/20251028-4/
3. e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 2 Report — HKMA — 28 Oct 2025 — read the Executive Summary and Sections 4-5 — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251028e4a1.pdf
4. e-HKD: A Policy and Design Perspective — HKMA — 27 Apr 2022 — read Sections 5.3-5.4 on privacy and intermediaries — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/financial-infrastructure/e-HKD_A_Policy_and_Design_Perspective.pdf

title: Project Ensemble
md:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA's) wholesale central bank digital currency (wCBDC) project for settling tokenised money between banks, now in a real-value pilot called EnsembleTX. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | HKMA, with an industry Architecture Community that advises on standards [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-3] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot (EnsembleTX is to operate throughout 2026) [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1, 3] |
| Started | 7 Mar 2024 [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1] |
| Next official date | Around end-2026: 24/7 operations and settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) under EnsembleTX (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [E1](#m-E1), [E2](#m-E2), [A3](#m-A3), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

Ensemble explores new market infrastructure so that banks can settle tokenised money with each other through wCBDC. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2]; [S:460620ab7f2b, footnote 1] Its first focus is tokenised deposits, meaning digital versions of ordinary commercial bank deposits. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] The HKMA set up an Architecture Community in May 2024 to develop shared industry standards. [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-2] A Sandbox followed in August 2024. Community banks connected their tokenised-deposit platforms to it, ready to run interbank PvP (payment versus payment) and DvP (delivery versus payment) experiments. [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1-2] In November 2025 the project moved to EnsembleTX, a pilot using real value. It starts with tokenised money market fund trades and real-time treasury and liquidity uses. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] At first, interbank settlement runs through the HKD RTGS (real-time gross settlement) system. The HKMA plans a gradual upgrade to round-the-clock settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 Mar 2024 | HKMA unveils Project Ensemble | Superseded (by EnsembleTX) | [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 1] |
| 7 May 2024 | Ensemble Architecture Community formed | Pilot (still a partner forum) | [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1, 3]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 4] |
| 27 Jun 2024 | HKMA and Banque de France (BDF) announce work, under a recent memorandum of understanding (MoU), on linking BDF's DL3S with the Ensemble Sandbox | Exploratory | [S:0ed273d6f63f, paras 2-3] |
| 28 Aug 2024 | Ensemble Sandbox launched, with four test themes | Superseded (by EnsembleTX) | [S:460620ab7f2b, paras 1, 3]; [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 2] |
| 28 Oct 2024 | Tie-ups with Banco Central do Brasil (BCB, Drex) and Bank of Thailand (BoT, Project San) | Exploratory | [S:8d9f12b43ada, para 1]; [S:aabff1db2350, paras 1, 3] |
| 13 Nov 2025 | EnsembleTX real-value pilot launched | Pilot | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget says the HKMA will keep upgrading EnsembleTX to support 24/7 settlement | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 109] |
| 2 Mar 2026 | MoU of the HKMA, Shanghai Data Bureau and a national blockchain centre; e-bills of lading to be explored under Ensemble | Exploratory | [S:eb28508e5032, paras 1-2] |
| Around end-2026 | 24/7 operations and CBDC settlement in EnsembleTX | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| By end-2026 | Pilot transactions for tokenised-deposit trade-finance use cases studied with the Mainland | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 99] |

## What it means for your bank

- The HKMA lists seven Tokenised Deposit Banks. It describes them as banks that are going to offer tokenised deposits to Hong Kong customers and settle interbank tokenised-deposit deals through EnsembleTX with real value. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A, p.1] The HKMA invites others with real-value use cases for tokenised deposits to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 5]
- When customers place tokenised deposits, the HKMA says banks should also meet its tokenised-products circular. That circular expects due diligence, disclosure, risk controls and discussion with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1, p.1; sections (A)-(C), pp.3-5; 'Implementation', p.6]
- For the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), a bank may treat qualifying tokenised deposits (a legally binding claim on it, redeemable at par) as deposits or unsecured funding. They cannot count as stable retail deposits. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, pp.89-90]
- The HKMA's non-binding note on distributed ledger technology (DLT) sets out what it would expect on network choice, smart contracts, legal risks such as settlement finality, and private-key security. [S:1884530ff235, Introduction, 4th bullet; items 2-4 and 8]
- Before a full launch, the Supervisory Incubator lets a bank check its risk controls with a dedicated HKMA team; tokenised deposits are a core focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** EnsembleTX is a pilot, not a rulebook. Customer tokenised deposits still fall under the HKMA tokenised-products circular, which expects discussion with the HKMA in advance. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1]; [S:b2719f3dcb37, footnote 1; 'Implementation', p.6]
- **To business heads:** The pilot starts with tokenised money market funds and real-time treasury uses, and the HKMA invites new real-value use cases for tokenised deposits. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 2 and 5]
- **To the CEO:** The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA plans to bring 24/7 operations and CBDC settlement to EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- **To Risk:** Tokenised deposits cannot get stable retail deposit LCR treatment. If holders cannot always be identified, they count as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4, p.89]

## Key documents

title: Project mBridge
md:
A shared platform on which several central banks issue their own central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), so that banks can settle cross-border payments and foreign exchange (FX) trades directly. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | The mBridge project team: the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the Bank of Thailand (BoT), the Digital Currency Institute of the People's Bank of China (PBC DCI), the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates (CBUAE) and the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub (BISIH) Hong Kong Centre. In June 2024 the Saudi Central Bank was welcomed as the next full participant. [S:db56d97e2206, footnote 1, para 3] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot (minimum viable product stage); the Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
| Started | Q4 2019 as Inthanon-LionRock; renamed in Feb 2021 [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and footnote 1] |
| Next official date | None stated; the Government says wider public and private participation will come gradually [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
| Covered in | [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The project began as Inthanon-LionRock, a CBDC study for cross-border payments started by the HKMA and the BoT. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and footnote 1] In February 2021 the PBC DCI and the CBUAE joined, and it was renamed the m-CBDC Bridge. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] The platform tests real-time, round-the-clock FX payment-versus-payment deals across several jurisdictions. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project mBridge' section] In the 2022 pilot, 20 banks in four jurisdictions made more than 160 payment and FX trades worth over US$22 million. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive summary, p.4] The platform reached minimum viable product (MVP) stage in June 2024, with a validating node in each founding central bank's jurisdiction. [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1-2] In October 2025 the Government told the Legislative Council (LegCo) that participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees for mBridge payments. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 2019 | Inthanon-LionRock (HKMA and BoT) | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, footnote 1] |
| Jan 2020 | Inthanon-LionRock report | Superseded | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section] |
| 23 Feb 2021 | PBC DCI and CBUAE join; renamed m-CBDC Bridge | Superseded | [S:6b0fae230518, para 1] |
| 28 Sep 2021 | Interim report on faster, cheaper payments | Research | [S:0cfb7eee08a3, paras 1, 3] |
| 15 Aug 2022 | Six-week real-value pilot begins | Pilot | [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.17] |
| 26 Oct 2022 | Pilot results published | Pilot | [S:2c7f151156dc, paras 1-2] |
| Oct 2023 | mBridge update brochure | Pilot | [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.1] |
| 5 Jun 2024 | MVP reached; Saudi Central Bank welcomed as next full participant | Pilot | [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1, 3] |
| 8 Oct 2025 | Government: mBridge is part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure | Pilot | [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Before sending or confirming a payment, each bank runs its own compliance checks, including anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and sanctions, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- Each participating bank must follow the AML, CTF and sanctions laws that apply to it. The platform only attaches a pass or fail certificate from the bank's off-platform check. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]
- Banks keep know-your-customer (KYC), AML and CFT (counter-financing of terrorism) compliance off the bridge, under each jurisdiction's rules. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]
- Foreign banks can hold and use another jurisdiction's CBDC, but only that jurisdiction's domestic banks can ask for it to be issued or redeemed. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, p.32]; [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.2]
- Private firms can propose add-on technology or use cases through a BISIH participation form. [S:db56d97e2206, para 4]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** On mBridge, AML and sanctions checks stay with each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30; s.7.2(d), p.35]
- **To business heads:** Participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees for mBridge payments. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- **To the CEO:** mBridge reached MVP in June 2024; the Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1]; [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- **To Risk:** The 2022 pilot ran on a centralised cloud in Hong Kong. The report says keeping data in one cloud raised privacy concerns. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33]

title: Government policy statements and Policy Address items
md:
The Government's own strategy papers on digital assets: the 2022 Policy Statement, Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) in 2025, and the digital-asset targets in the 2025 and 2026 Policy Addresses. [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6, date line]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 2, 4]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) for the policy statements; Chief Executive for Policy Addresses [S:f587b828e3fa, opening paragraph, p.1]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 2]; [S:ef3648ff1610, cover page] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Stated target (Policy Statement 2.0 and 2026 Policy Address); 2022 statement superseded by Policy Statement 2.0, which builds on it [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 3-4] |
| Started | 31 Oct 2022 [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6, date line] |
| Next official date | Bill on virtual asset (VA) dealing, custody, advisory and management to be introduced in 2026 (stated target) [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| Covered in | [A3](#m-A3), [A1](#m-A1), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The 2022 Policy Statement adopted the principle of treating the same activity and risks under the same regulation. It also announced work on a licensing regime for VA service providers. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6] It listed three pilots: a non-fungible token (NFT) issue, a tokenised Government green bond and e-HKD. [S:f587b828e3fa, para 10] Policy Statement 2.0 (PS 2.0, June 2025) set out the LEAP framework. LEAP means legal and regulatory streamlining, expanding tokenised products, advancing use cases and cross-sector collaboration, and people and partnership development. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 4] It proposed the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) as lead authority for licensing and registering digital-asset dealing and custody providers, with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] It also switched the Government's term to *digital assets*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] *Virtual asset* remains the term defined in the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). [S:7395a53cc85a, Note] The 2026 Policy Address adds targets for the HKMA and SFC, some with dates. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35, 49-50]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 Oct 2022 | Policy Statement on Development of VA in Hong Kong | Superseded | [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6, date line]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 3] |
| 26 Jun 2025 | Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) | Stated target | [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] |
| 17 Sep 2025 | 2025 Policy Address: bill for dealing and custodian licensing in 2026 | Stated target | [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex item 22] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | 2026-27 Budget restates the 2026 bill target and plans a Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) amendment bill | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | 2026 Policy Address: tokenised Exchange Fund Bills tests by year-end; CMU OmniClear digital asset platform this year | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii), (iv)] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | 2026 Policy Address: SFC to widen VA licensing, tokenised gold, stablecoin trading | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(i)-(iii)] |
| Around end-2026 | EnsembleTX: settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) and round-the-clock operation | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] |
| By 2029 | Customs and Excise Department analytics systems for digital-asset transactions (DATAS) and anti-money laundering (AMLAS) | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209] |

## What it means for your bank

- PS 2.0 said the HKMA would be the frontline regulator for banks, supervising their digital-asset dealing and custody, with the SFC as lead licensing and registration authority. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- The 2025 Policy Address said the HKMA would encourage banks to introduce tokenised deposits, and would promote live deals such as settling tokenised money market funds with them. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40]
- The same paragraph said the HKMA would encourage banks to use the supervisory sandbox to improve their risk management. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, para 103, p.40]
- Separately, the HKMA expects each Authorized Institution's board to oversee and endorse a strategic business plan on technology change within six months of its 9 March 2026 circular. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4, pp.1-2]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Government now says *digital assets*, but *virtual asset* is still the defined term in AMLO. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]; [S:7395a53cc85a, Note]
- **To business heads:** The 2026 Policy Address says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms and their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- **To the CEO:** The Government's stated 2026 target is one bill for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management licensing. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- **To Risk:** Customs plans a digital-asset transaction analytics system by 2029, as part of its anti-money laundering big-data platform. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]

title: Relevant Stablecoins: dealing, advice and trading
md:
The May 2026 Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) package that eases how virtual-asset conduct rules apply to stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers, plus the stated plan for trading on licensed platforms.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for banks; Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for trading platforms and licensed corporations [S:a0bd48559762, opening paragraph, p.1]; [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph, p.1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (since 27 May 2026) [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| Started | 27 May 2026 [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] |
| Next official date | None fixed. Policy Address says the SFC will promote stablecoin trading on licensed platforms (stated target) [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |
| Covered in | [C1](#m-C1), [C4](#m-C4), [B2](#m-B2), [C7](#m-C7), [E1](#m-E1) |
## What it is

A Relevant Stablecoin is a specified stablecoin whose issue is authorised under a Stablecoins Ordinance licence. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] After the Ordinance started, the two regulators reviewed how the joint virtual-asset (VA) circulars should apply to these coins, given their currency-pegged profile. [S:a0bd48559762, Background, pp.1-2] The HKMA's circular to registered institutions (RIs) sets out the changes, with updated terms and conditions in Appendices A1 and A2. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance', p.2] A separate HKMA letter points all Authorized Institutions (AIs) to the same standards. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] The SFC's circular 26EC26 covers VA trading platforms (VATPs) and licensed corporations (LCs), and refers RIs to the HKMA circular. [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph and fn 2, p.1] The HKMA letter says its guidance should not be read as treating these coins as investment products. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Aug 2025 | Stablecoins Ordinance commences | In force | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| 10 Apr 2026 | First two issuer licences take effect | In force | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] |
| 27 May 2026 | HKMA RI circular with Appendices A1/A2 | In force | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| 27 May 2026 | HKMA letter to all AIs | In force | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| 27 May 2026 | SFC circular 26EC26 to VATPs and LCs | In force | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1, opening paragraph] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: SFC to promote stablecoin trading on licensed platforms and use in settling tokenised money market funds | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- An RI may now deal in a Relevant Stablecoin through the licensed issuer as well as through a VATP. [S:a0bd48559762, para (1), p.3]
- Relevant-Stablecoin-only dealing needs no Type 1 registration, but the Appendix A1 conduct terms still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, para (2), p.3]
- For accounts clearly ring-fenced as Relevant-Stablecoin-only, no VA knowledge test is needed. Adding any other VA brings back the full rules. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
- When dealing or advising, the bank should disclose material information on each coin's stabilisation mechanism and redemption arrangements. [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5; para (10), p.7]
- Advice should rest on thorough analysis, such as the client's use case. Commission rebates or other benefits should not be the main reason to recommend a coin. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- The HKMA reminds RIs to give it and the SFC advance notice before starting these activities or materially changing them. All AIs are reminded to discuss these activities with the HKMA in advance. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, 'Implementation', p.2]
- The changes do not apply to other stablecoins. The joint-circular rules and this circular also do not apply to AIs that are not RIs, or to a licensed issuer for its own coin; the HKMA expects these to meet similar standards it issues separately. [S:a0bd48559762, 'Detailed guidance' and footnote 3, p.2]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** As an RI, we follow the HKMA RI circular; 26EC26 sets standards for VATPs and LCs. RIs are still reminded to notify both regulators in advance. [S:19d52ade6849, opening paragraph and fn 2, p.1]; [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- **To business heads:** For Relevant-Stablecoin-only clients, no VA knowledge test and no VA exposure limit are needed. Offering those clients any other VA brings back the full rules. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)-(b) and fn 4, pp.4-5]
- **To the CEO:** The Policy Address says the SFC will promote licensed-platform trading of regulated stablecoins, including for tokenised money market fund settlement. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- **To Risk:** Only coins issued under an HKMA licence qualify, and the HKMA register lists the licensees. [S:19d52ade6849, para 2]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 4]

## Key documents

1. Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins (RI circular) — HKMA — 27 May 2026 — read all nine pages, especially paras (1)-(9) and Implementation — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf
2. Relevant Stablecoin-related Activities (letter to AIs) — HKMA — 27 May 2026 — read both pages — https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-4-EN/20260527-4-EN.pdf

title: Stablecoin issuer regime (Stablecoins Ordinance, Cap. 656)
md:
Hong Kong's licensing law for issuers of fiat-referenced stablecoins, from the 2024 sandbox through the Ordinance, the first licences, the public register, the review tribunal and complaint handling.

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as licensing authority [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]; a Stablecoin Review Tribunal, whose page is kept by the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB), reviews specified HKMA decisions [S:16699fe49364, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | In force (since 1 Aug 2025) [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Started | HKMA discussion paper, 12 Jan 2022 [S:2b888e600616, cover page and Section 6] |
| Next official date | None fixed. Launch of licensed coins was expected between mid-2026 and the second half of 2026, based on the issuers' business plans [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, first paragraph] |
| Covered in | [C4](#m-C4), [B2](#m-B2), [C3](#m-C3), [D1](#m-D1), [D3](#m-D3), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The Ordinance requires a business that issues a fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) in Hong Kong to hold an HKMA licence. The same applies to an FRS referenced to the Hong Kong dollar, wherever it is issued. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] A licensee must keep a separate reserve pool for each coin type, and that pool's market value must always be at least the par value of the coins in circulation. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1] Holders must have a right to redeem at par. Valid requests should be processed within one business day unless the HKMA approves otherwise. [S:240be6833157, paras 3.3.1, 3.3.3] Only permitted offerors may offer these coins, and an Authorized Institution (AI) is one of them. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1] The HKMA licensed the first two issuers with effect from 10 April 2026. It says that if more licences are granted, the total will remain very limited. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1]; [S:193316443831, 'Follow-up work', para 3]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 Jan 2022 | HKMA discussion paper on crypto-assets and stablecoins | Superseded | [S:2b888e600616, cover page and Section 6] |
| 27 Dec 2023 | FSTB–HKMA consultation on issuer regime (comments to 29 Feb 2024) | Superseded | [S:167649d1bc28, cover page and para 3] |
| 12 Mar 2024 | Stablecoin issuer sandbox launched | Superseded | [S:f2a668eb3b93, para 1] |
| 17 Jul 2024 | Consultation conclusions published | Superseded | [S:54aa01e7396e, cover page and para 12.1] |
| 18 Jul 2024 | First sandbox participants announced (three entries, one a group of three firms) | Superseded | [S:cf1df12c1b58, para 1] |
| 6 Dec 2024 | Stablecoins Bill gazetted | Superseded | [S:a9a82f2b38ce, para 1] |
| 21 May 2025 | Legislative Council (LegCo) passes the Bill | Superseded | [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 1] |
| 1 Aug 2025 | Ordinance and HKMA guidelines take effect | In force | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]; [S:6c3f349e4f90, para 1] |
| 1 Nov 2025 | Current Stablecoin Review Tribunal membership term begins (to 31 Oct 2028) | In force | [S:16699fe49364, para 2] |
| 10 Apr 2026 | First two issuer licences take effect; HKMA points the public to its register | In force | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 1, 4] |
| Mid-to-late 2026 | Launch of licensed coins expected | Stated target | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply, first paragraph] |

## What it means for your bank

- As a permitted offeror, the bank may offer coins from licensed issuers to retail and professional investors. Other specified stablecoins may go to professional investors only. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]
- An AI can apply to issue. An AI incorporated overseas needs no local subsidiary, and some minimum criteria, such as financial resources, do not apply to AI applicants. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 8]
- The HKMA keeps a public register of licensees and tells the public to use it to check claims about them. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]
- Sandbox admission did not mean HKMA endorsement, and participants had to apply separately for a licence. [S:f2a668eb3b93, Annex, Objectives, p.1]
- For its own holdings, the bank must notify the HKMA when it acquires a new type of cryptoasset, and treat it as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees its classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- The HKMA may assess complaints about an issuer that the issuer has not handled properly. It generally does not order an issuer to pay compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, 'Lodging Complaint with the HKMA' section]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Only coins from licensed issuers may be offered to retail investors, and AIs are permitted offerors. The HKMA register lists who is licensed. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]
- **To business heads:** Two issuers hold licences effective 10 April 2026. The HKMA says any further licences will stay very limited in number. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, 'Follow-up work', para 3]
- **To the CEO:** An AI may apply to issue, and the financial-resources and business-activities criteria do not apply to it. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.2.1; fns 1, 8]
- **To Risk:** A licensee must give holders a right to redeem at par, and should process valid requests within one business day. Reserves should be held under trust arrangements with qualified custodians. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.5.2, 2.5.4, 3.3.1, 3.3.3]

title: Supervisory Incubator for DLT
md:
A Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) arrangement where a bank can check its risk controls for a distributed ledger technology (DLT) initiative with a dedicated HKMA team before full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Pilot: Authorized Institutions (AIs) may apply for access [S:fae36c380174, p.1; p.2]; still promoted by the HKMA in March 2026 [S:38e1f67c38df, para 3] |
| Started | 8 Jan 2025 [S:fae36c380174, p.1] |
| Next official date | None stated |
| Covered in | [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3), [C5](#m-C5), [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

The Incubator is a supervisory arrangement to help banks manage the risks of adopting DLT. It pays particular attention to risks in services that span DLT and legacy systems. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] Tokenised deposits were a core focus from the start. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2] For a single bank, it offers one contact point to reconfirm that risk controls are adequate before launch, with a dedicated HKMA team and optional live trials. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Trials are run in a hands-on, step-by-step way. [S:fae36c380174, p.1] At industry level, it is to share good practice through guidance, sharing sessions and research. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 4] In an HKMA inSight article of 24 October 2025, the HKMA said six banks had launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 Apr 2024 | HKMA issues non-binding DLT risk-management considerations | In force | [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction] |
| 8 Jan 2025 | Incubator launched at FiNETech4; circular to AIs | Pilot | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 1, 6]; [S:fae36c380174, p.1] |
| 24 Oct 2025 | HKMA reports six banks' tokenised deposit services launched via the Incubator | Pilot | [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section] |
| 9 Mar 2026 | Business-model circular says banks' plans may include small real-world trials through the Incubator | In force | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |
| 9 Mar 2026 | HKMA event on Project Ensemble and the Incubator for around 60 banks | Pilot | [S:38e1f67c38df, para 3 and closing note] |

## What it means for your bank

- Access is voluntary: AIs that want to use the Incubator contact the HKMA. [S:fae36c380174, p.2] Its purpose is to reconfirm risk controls before a full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]
- The HKMA is prepared to give AIs in the Incubator some supervisory flexibility, assessed case by case. One factor is whether the bank can meet operating principles similar to those for Fintech Supervisory Sandbox (FSS) trials. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2]
- That flexibility rests on the bank managing trial risks in line with the trial's scale, scope and nature. [S:fae36c380174, p.1]
- Where an existing rule does not fit DLT well and that mismatch is inadvertent, or runs against the "same activity, same risk, same regulation" principle, the HKMA says it will consider whether regulatory adaptations or flexibility are needed. [S:fae36c380174, p.2]
- The HKMA's non-binding DLT considerations remain a reference: board responsibility, network choice, smart contracts, legal risks such as settlement finality, and private key security. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction; items 1-4, 8]
- AIs planning new digital-asset activities are expected to discuss them with the HKMA before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Any supervisory flexibility in the Incubator is decided case by case and depends on how the bank manages trial risks. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and footnote 2]
- **To business heads:** Six banks have launched tokenised deposit services through the Incubator, according to the HKMA. [S:418769c01edc, 'Supervisory Incubator for DLT – where traditional finance and tokenisation meets' section]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA's business-model circular says a bank's strategic plan may factor in small real-world trials through the Incubator. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- **To Risk:** The HKMA's DLT considerations say the board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]

title: Tokenised Bond Expert Group and the DLT fixed-income law review
md:
An HKMA industry panel on tokenised bonds, working alongside a joint FSTB–HKMA review of whether Hong Kong's legal and regulatory regime supports using distributed ledger technology (DLT) in the bond market. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1, 3]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 1]

## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Run by | Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for the Tokenised Bond Expert Group (TBEG); Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and HKMA for the review [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] |
| Status as of 25 Sep 2026 | Exploratory (TBEG); review phase 1 conclusions published 29 Jun 2026 [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-3]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] |
| Started | Review first announced in the 2025-26 Budget; TBEG held its first discussions in May 2026 and was announced on 5 Jun 2026 [S:279f10054c6e, para 15]; [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1, 3] |
| Next official date | Phase 2 legal review in H2 2026 (stated target) [S:279f10054c6e, para 8]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |
| Covered in | [C5](#m-C5), [A3](#m-A3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3) |
## What it is

Policy Statement 2.0 said the FSTB and HKMA would lead a legal and regulatory review on tokenisation, with an initial focus on bonds. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 9] The 2026-27 Budget said the Government would issue guidance confirming that registers of debenture holders may be kept on a distributed ledger. It also said it would explore e-signatures for bond documents and digitised bearer bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107] The HKMA announced the TBEG on 5 June 2026. Its members come from industry bodies, financial institutions, law firms and infrastructure and technology providers. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2] The group's May 2026 discussions fed into the joint review. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 3] Phase 1 concluded that current law and regulation are already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. [S:279f10054c6e, para 1] On the same day, the Companies Registry published FAQs. They confirm that a DLT-based register of debenture holders can meet Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) record-keeping rules. [S:279f10054c6e, para 6]

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26 Jun 2025 | Policy Statement 2.0 commits to a tokenisation law review, starting with bonds | Stated target | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 9] |
| 25 Feb 2026 | Budget sets review directions: DLT registers, e-signatures, bearer bonds | Stated target | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 107]; [S:279f10054c6e, para 15] |
| May 2026 | First TBEG discussion sessions | Exploratory | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 3] |
| 5 Jun 2026 | HKMA announces the TBEG | Exploratory | [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 1] |
| 29 Jun 2026 | Phase 1 findings and Companies Registry FAQs | Conclusions published | [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 6] |
| H2 2026 | Phase 2 legislative review (e-execution; possession and transfer of tokens) | Stated target | [S:279f10054c6e, paras 8-11] |
| 16 Sep 2026 | Policy Address: TBEG to launch the phase 2 review with the FSTB | Stated target | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iii)] |

## What it means for your bank

- Phase 1 created no new obligation. It found the current legal and regulatory environment already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 3]
- If the bank keeps or relies on a DLT debenture register for a Hong Kong company, the Companies Registry FAQs are the reference point. [S:279f10054c6e, para 6]
- Phase 2 will look at electronic signatures for trusts linked to tokenised bonds and funds. It will also look at how possession and transfer work for tokenised fixed-income instruments. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 9-11]
- The HKMA says it will review and update the group's membership when needed. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 4]

## Talking points

- **To the CCO:** Phase 1 changed no law; it confirmed flexibility and added Companies Registry FAQs on DLT registers. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 1, 6]
- **To business heads:** Phase 2 will explore electronic execution of tokenised bond issue documents, aimed at a more efficient and automated issuance process. [S:279f10054c6e, para 10]
- **To the CEO:** The HKMA set up the TBEG to explore policy measures, market practices and innovations with industry. [S:fc3eb72031c6, paras 1-2]
- **To Risk:** Possession and transfer of tokenised instruments are topics for the phase 2 review, set for H2 2026. [S:279f10054c6e, paras 8, 11]

1. FSTB and HKMA to further unlock potential of DLT in Hong Kong's fixed income market — FSTB and HKMA — 29 Jun 2026 — read the whole release, especially 'Next phase' — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/06/20260629-4/
2. HKMA establishes Tokenised Bond Expert Group — HKMA — 5 Jun 2026 — read paras 1-4 and the Annex of members — https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/06/20260605-3/
